title: Bacteria, archaea, and viruses are not one kind of thing
summary: OpenStax Microbiology distinguishes bacteria from archaea and notes that viruses are much smaller.
body: OpenStax Microbiology, section 1.3, treats archaea and bacteria as distinct groups of cells and says bacterial cells are typically about 1 micrometre while viruses can be about ten times smaller. A virus is not a small bacterium. Antimicrobial drugs and vaccines are matched to the kind of microbe. WHO's antimicrobial-resistance page includes viruses among microbes that can stop responding to the drugs aimed at them; that is a different claim from the classroom rule about which drugs are antibacterial.
